newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco Teniente union talks said amiable.
newsitem.headline: Codelco Teniente union talks said amiable.

text.p: Preliminary wage talks between Codelco-Chile's El Teniente copper mine and its workers below the rank of supervisor are progressing amiably but are still about 10 days away from any concrete proposals from either side, a Codelco official said Monday.
"I think it will be about 10 days before one side or the other comes up with anything at all concrete," the Teniente official told Reuters. "But there is good will in the talks, and no tension."

He said six unions representing 6,300 of Teniente's 6,490 employees had agreed to a management proposal to avoid possible distractions from parliamentary elections. He added that they agreed to try to agree to a new collective wage contract before the present accord expires in December.
Collective wage contracts must last for at least two years under Chilean law, but may be longer.
El Teniente mined 342,800 tonnes of copper last year and is state- owned Codelco's second largest mine, after Chuquicamata.

Chile's copper mining industry -- the world's largest -- has over the past year or so been hit by strikes at mines including Chuquicamata, and at the privately-owned Escondida and Quebrada Blanca pits.
